34:["$","p",null,{"className":"x:not-first:mt-[1.25em] x:leading-7","children":["Then cache ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":".ttsc-cache/ttsc/plugins"}]," as the required artifact. Add ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":".ttsc-cache/ttsc/go-build"}]," only as the optional accelerator. The same variable places temporary ttsx output under ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":".ttsc-cache/ttsc/ttsx"}],", so a nested tsconfig cannot create a second project-local cache root. Point the root at a directory dedicated to ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsc"}]," whose basename is ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsc"}],": ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsc clean"}]," always removes its ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"plugins/"}],", and that basename is the safety proof that lets it remove the nested ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"go-build/"}]," too. A shared location such as ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"~/.cache"}]," is therefore the wrong target. Keep the root, and ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"TTSC_GO_CACHE_DIR"}],", outside every plugin’s Go sources as well: a plugin binary is keyed on its sources, so a build refuses a cache inside them instead of changing the sources it was keyed on while it builds. A project whose root is itself a plugin’s Go module therefore needs a root elsewhere, or below its ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"node_modules"}],", which the sources never include."]}]
35:["$","p",null,{"className":"x:not-first:mt-[1.25em] x:leading-7","children":["Relocating costs you automatic cleanup. In the default project-local cache, ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsc"}]," prunes plugin binaries unused for 30 days and runs LRU pruning from a 2 GiB ceiling toward 1.6 GiB. The same policy covers ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"descriptors"}],", ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"capabilities"}],", and ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsx-orphan"}],", where every reuse of an entry records a use, so an answer launches keep reading is not evicted by its age. It checks at most daily while idle and again after every cold binary publication, so a fresh daily marker cannot hide the binary just added. The binary returned by that cold build and entries with active build generations are excluded; if those safety exclusions keep the root above the ceiling, the marker schedules another pass instead of deleting an entry that may be about to execute. ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsc"}]," applies the corresponding policy to the Go object cache after every cold source-plugin build attempt, including a failed build, pruning from an 8 GiB ceiling toward 6 GiB. The newest target-sized Go-object cohort remains protected for the requested hour plus Go’s one-hour access-mtime coalescing tolerance. Active builds and maintenance publish heartbeat records. A stopped build heartbeat retains a one-hour grace for an orphaned Go child; completed maintenance is retired immediately, and an abandoned maintenance heartbeat expires after one minute. A record dated implausibly far in the future is rebased and receives one ordinary grace period: a live owner refreshes it, while an orphan then expires normally. A root named explicitly through ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"TTSC_CACHE_DIR"}]," or ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"--cache-dir"}]," is never garbage collected, on the assumption that a caller who named a path owns it. For a ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"TTSC_CACHE_DIR"}]," root, ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsc clean"}]," removes its ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"plugins"}],", ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"descriptors"}],", ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"capabilities"}],", and ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsx-orphan"}],", the ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsx"}]," runtime directories whose recorded owners are provably gone, and the nested ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"go-build"}]," when the basename is ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsc"}],". It keeps and reports the runtime directory of a run that may still be in progress, one whose process is alive or ran on another host, and keeps one without an owner record, which may belong to a live run of an earlier release. ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"ttsc clean --cache-dir <dir>"}]," removes the named directory wholesale, a run still using it included. ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"TTSC_GO_CACHE_DIR"}]," follows the same caller-owned lifetime, and an ambient user ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"GOCACHE"}]," is never modified or removed by ttsc."]}]
36:["$","p",null,{"className":"x:not-first:mt-[1.25em] x:leading-7","children":"An owner record that cannot be read or parsed, or a run with no owner record from an older release, leaves ownership unknown, so default clean keeps that run. If the run index itself cannot be listed, clean fails without removing the runtime directory. A new run’s directory and owner record are published under the same lock that default clean holds while it chooses and removes old runs. The run index is pinned to its physical directory before ownership is inspected, so changing a cache link later cannot redirect removal to another run. A dangling link at the runtime root is removed as a link. Each Node child that inherits the runtime manifest records its own ownership before running user code; a live descendant keeps the run’s output after its launcher exits. A child without that manifest uses its own dependency cache and does not claim the parent run."}]

40:["$","p",null,{"className":"x:not-first:mt-[1.25em] x:leading-7","children":["An ephemeral builder (Google Cloud Build, most CI Docker builds) discards its local layer and BuildKit cache between builds, so the warm layer is reused only through a cache that outlives the build: a registry-backed layer cache (",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"docker build --cache-from <pushed-image> --build-arg BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1"}],", then deploy the built image) or a bucket-backed cache. ",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"gcloud run deploy --source"}]," passes no cache flag and, under buildpacks, offers no layer to hold the binary; to reuse it you must take over the build (",["$","code",null,{"className":"nextra-code","dir":"ltr","children":"gcloud builds submit"}]," with a registry cache, or a prebuilt base image) rather than deploy from source."]}]
